memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant law in his hands. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back. The tablets were the work of God; the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets." - Exod 32:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pause on this detail. These were not tablets Moses carved and God dictated. The stone was God's work. The writing was God's writing. Every letter came from His own hand.

Scripture is placing enormous weight on this. God's law is not a human invention or a committee's opinion about morality. It came from God Himself. That is why the coming clash is so severe — the very moment God's own handwriting is descending the mountain, His people are dancing before gold.

There is comfort here too. We do not follow guesses. The God who speaks has actually spoken, first through prophets and finally through His Son (Heb 1:1-2). When you open your Bible, you are not reading advice. You are hearing from God.

And here is the wonder of the gospel: what was once engraved on stone, God now promises to write on human hearts (Jer 31:33; 2 Cor 3:3). Stone can be shattered. A heart transformed by the Spirit carries the law within.

Do you treat Scripture as God's word — or as one voice among many competing for your attention?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does your handling of Scripture show what you believe about its author?
2. Is God's Word written on your heart, or only kept on your shelf?
3. What is one command of God you have been treating as optional?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You have spoken. Write Your Word deep into my heart by Your Spirit. Amen.
